verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              श्रुता मे कथताः पूर्वे चत्वारो मानवाश्रमाः। व्याख्यानयित्वा व्याख्यानमेषामाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Thus addressed by his father, Shuka, highly praising these instructions of the great Rishi, began to ask the following questions regarding the import of duties which brings on Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              विदिताः सर्व एवेह धर्मास्तव युधिष्ठिर। यथा मम महाबाहो विदिताः साधुसम्मताः॥२॥
verses.english: Shuka said By what means does a wise man well-read in the Vedas, observant of sacrifices, and shorn of malice attains to Brahma which is incapable of being apprehended by either direct evidence or inference, and incapable of being described by the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: यत्तु लिङ्गान्तरगतं पृच्छसे मां युधिष्ठिर। धर्मं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ तन्निबोध नराधिप॥३॥
verses.english: Asked by me, tell me by what means can Brahma be known. Is it by penance, by Brahmacharya, by renunciation of everything, by intelligence, by help of the Sankhya philosophy, or by the Yoga?

verses.sanskrit: सर्वाण्येतानि कौन्तेय विद्यन्ते मनुजर्षभ। साध्वाचारप्रवृत्तानां चातुराश्रम्यकारिणाम्॥४॥
verses.english: What are the means and what sort of singleness of purpose may inen acquire regarding both, viz., the mind and the senses? You should explain all this to me!

verses.sanskrit: अकामद्वेषयुक्तस्य दण्डनीत्या युधिष्ठिर। समदर्शिनश्च भूतेषु भैक्ष्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥५॥
verses.english: Vyasa said No man achieves success by any other means save the acquisition of knowledge, the practice of penances, the control of the senses, and renunciation of everything.

verses.sanskrit: वेत्ति ज्ञानविसर्गं च निग्रहानुग्रहं तथा। यथोक्तवृत्तेर्धीरस्य क्षेमाश्रमपदं भवेत्॥६॥
verses.english: The great elements (five in number) represent the first creation of the Self-create. They have been very largely put in embodied creatures living in the world of life.

verses.sanskrit: अर्हान्पूजयतो नित्यं संविभागेन पाण्डव। सर्वतस्तस्य कौन्तेय भैक्ष्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥७॥
verses.english: The bodies of all embodied creatures are originated from earth. Their humours originate from water. Their eyes originate from light. Prana, Apana (and other vital breaths), depend on the wind. And, lastly, all unoccupied apertures within them originate from Space.

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञातिसम्बन्धिमित्राणि व्यापन्नानि युधिष्ठिर। समभ्युद्धरमाणस्य दीक्षाश्रमपदं भवेत्॥८॥
verses.english: Vishnu is in the feet (of living creatures). Indra is in their arms. Within the stomach lies Agni, desirous of eating. The points of the horizon are in the ears, the organ of hearing. Speech, which is the goddess of learning, is in the tongue.

verses.sanskrit: लोकमुख्येषु सत्कारं लिङ्गिमुख्येषु चासकृत्। कुर्वतस्तस्य कौन्तेय वन्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥९॥
verses.english: The ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose forming the fifth, are the senses of knowledge. These exist for apprehending their respective objects.

verses.sanskrit: आह्निकं पितृयज्ञांश्च भूतयज्ञान्समानुषान्। कुर्वतः पार्थ विपुलान्वन्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१०॥
verses.english: Sound, touch, from, taste, and scent for the fifth, are the objects of the (five) senses. These should always be considered as distinct from the senses.

verses.sanskrit: संविभागेन भूतानामतिथीनां तथार्चनात्। देवयज्ञैश्च राजेन्द्र वन्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥११॥
मर्दनं परराष्ट्राणां शिष्टार्थं सत्यविक्रम। कुर्वतः पुरुषव्याघ्र वन्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१२॥
पालनात्सर्वभूतानां स्वराष्ट्रपरिपालनात्। दीक्षा बहुविधा राजन्सत्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१३॥
वेदाध्ययननित्यत्वं क्षमाऽथाचार्यपूजनम्। अथोपाध्यायशुश्रूषा ब्रह्माश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१४॥
आह्निकं जपमानस्य देवान्पूजयतः सदा। धर्मेण पुरुषव्याघ्र धर्माश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१५॥
मृत्युर्वा रक्षणं वेति यस्य राज्ञो विनिश्चयः। प्राणद्यूते ततस्तस्य ब्रह्माश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१६॥
अजिह्ममशठं मार्गं वर्तमानस्य भारत। सर्वदा सर्वभूतेषु ब्रह्माश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१७॥
वानप्रस्थेषु विप्रेषु त्रैविद्येषु च भारत। प्रयच्छतोऽर्थान्विपुलान्वन्याश्रमपदं भवेत्॥१८॥
सर्वभूतेष्वनुक्रोशं कुर्वतस्तस्य भारत। आनृशंस्यप्रवृत्तस्य सर्वावस्थं पदं भवेत्॥१९॥
बालवृद्धेषु कौन्तेय सर्वावस्थं युधिष्ठिर। अनुक्रोशक्रिया पार्थ सर्वावस्थं पदं भवेत्॥२०॥
बलात्कृतेषु भूतेषु परित्राणं कुरूद्वह। शरणागतेषु कौरव्य कुर्वन्गार्हस्थ्यमावसेत्॥२१॥
चराचराणां भूतानां रक्षणं चापि सर्वशः। यथार्हपूजां च तथा कुर्वन्गार्हस्थ्यमावसेत्॥२२॥
ज्येष्ठानुज्येष्ठपत्नीनां भ्रातॄणां पुत्रनप्तॄणाम्। निग्रहानुग्रहौ पार्थ गार्हस्थ्यमिति तत्तपः॥२३॥
साधूनामर्चनीयानां पूजासु विदितात्मनाम्। पालनं पुरुषव्याघ्र गृहाश्रमपदं भवेत्॥२४॥
आश्रमस्थानि भूतानि यस्तु वेश्मनि भारत। आददीतेह भोज्येन तद्गार्हस्थ्यं युधिष्ठिर॥२५॥
यः स्थितः पुरुषो धर्मे धात्रा सृष्टे यथार्थवत्। आश्रमाणां हि सर्वेषां फलं प्राप्नोत्यनामयम्॥२६॥
यस्मिन्न नश्यन्ति गुणाः कौन्तेय पुरुषे सदा। आश्रमस्थं तमप्याहुर्नरश्रेष्ठं युधिष्ठिर॥२७॥
स्थानमानं कुले मानं वयोमानं तथैव च। कुर्वन्वसति सर्वेषु ह्याश्रमेषु युधिष्ठिर॥२८॥
देशधर्मांश्च कौन्तेय कुलधर्मांस्तथैव च। पालयन्पुरुषव्याघ्र राजा सर्वाश्रमी भवेत्॥२९॥
काले विभूतिं भूतानामुपहारांस्तथैव च। अर्हयन्पुरुषव्याघ्र साधूनामाश्रमे वसेत्॥३०॥
verses.english: That is minuter than the minutest, and is the heart of all things. Though existing, that is still imperceptible.

verses.sanskrit: दशधर्मगतश्चापि यो धर्मं प्रत्यवेक्षते। सर्वलोकस्य कौन्तेय राजा भवति सोऽश्रमी॥३१॥
verses.english: Indestructible and destructible,-these are the dual forms of the (Supreme) Self. The existence it shows in all mobile and immobile entities is destructible; while the existence in shows in Chaitanya is celestial, immortal, and indestructible.

verses.sanskrit: ये धर्मकुशला लोके धर्मं कुर्वन्ति भारत। पालिता यस्य विषये धर्मांशस्तस्य भूपतेः॥३२॥
verses.english: Though the master of all existent beings both mobile and immobile, though inactive and shorn of attributes, it enters nevertheless the well-known house of nine doors and becomes engaged in action.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मारामान्धर्मपरान्ये न रक्षन्ति मानवान्। पार्थिवाः पुरुषव्याघ्र तेषां पापं हरन्ति ते॥३३॥
verses.english: Wise men who can see the other shore hold that the Supreme Soul becomes endued with the attribute of action on account of motion, pleasure and pain, variety of form, and the nine well-known possessions.

verses.sanskrit: ये चाप्यत्र सहायाः स्युः पार्थिवानां युधिष्ठिर। ते चैवांशहराः सर्वे धर्मे परकृतेऽनघ॥३४॥
verses.english: That indestructible Soul which is said to be endued with the attribute or action is nothing else than the indestructible Soul which is said to be inactive. A learned person, by attaining to that indestructible essence, gives up for ever both life and birth.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वाश्रमपदेऽप्याहुर्गार्हस्थ्यं दीप्तनिर्णयम्। पावनं पुरुषव्याघ्र यं धर्मं पर्युपास्महे॥३५॥
verses.english: The learned declare that the Garhasthya, which we follow, is superior to all the other modes of life. The conclusions regarding it are very clear. It is certainly sacred, O foremost of men.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मोपमस्तु भूतेषु यो वै भवति मानवः। न्यस्तदण्डो जितक्रोधः प्रेत्येह लभते सुखम्॥३६॥
verses.english: That man, who regards all creatures as his own self, who never does any harm and has his anger under control, enjoys great happiness both here and here after.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मे स्थिता सत्त्ववीर्या धर्मसेतुवटारका। त्यागवाताध्वगा शीघ्रा नौस्तं संतारयिष्यति॥३७॥
verses.english: A king can easily cross the ocean of the world having kingly duties as his fleet boat urged on by the breeze of gifts,, having the scriptures for its tackle and intelligence for the strength of its helmsman, and kept afloat by the power of virtue.

verses.sanskrit: यदा निवृत्तः सर्वस्मात् कामो योऽस्य हृदि स्थितः। तदा भवति सत्त्वस्थस्ततो ब्रह्म समश्नुते॥३८॥
verses.english: When all attachment for every earthly object, is withdrawn from his heart he is then regarded as one leaving in his understanding alone. In this state he soon attains to Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: सुप्रसन्नस्तु भावेन योगेन च नराधिप। धर्मं पुरुषशार्दूल प्राप्स्यते पालने रतः॥३९॥
verses.english: Becoming cheerful by meditation and by controlling desire and other passions of the heart, O foremost of men, a king, engaged in discharging the duty of protection, succeeds in acquiring great merit.

verses.sanskrit: वेदाध्ययनशीलानां विप्राणां साधुकर्मणाम्। पालने यत्नमातिष्ठ सर्वलोकस्य चैव ह॥४०॥
verses.english: Do you, therefore, O Yudhishthira, try your best to protect Brahmanas of pious deeds and devoted to the study of the Vedas, as also all other men.

verses.sanskrit: वने चरन्ति ये धर्ममाश्रमेषु च भारत। रक्षणात्तच्छतगुणं धर्मं प्राप्नोति पार्थिवः॥४१॥
verses.english: By following the duty of protection only, o Bharata, the king acquires merit that is a hundred times greater than what is earned by hermits in their asylums in the forest.

verses.sanskrit: एष ते विविधो धर्मः पाण्डवश्रेष्ठ कीर्तितः। अनुतिष्ठ त्वमेनं वै पूर्वदृष्टं सनातनम्॥४२॥
verses.english: I have now described, O eldest son of Pandu, the various duties of men. Do you follow kingly duties which are eternal and that have been practised by great men since days of yore.

verses.sanskrit: चातुराश्रम्यमैकाग्र्यं चातुर्वर्यं च पाण्डव। धर्मं पुरुषशार्दूल प्राप्स्यसे पालने रतः॥४३॥
verses.english: If you devote yourself head and soul to the duty of protecting (your subjects), O foremost of men, you may then, O son of Pandu, acquire the merits of all the four modes of life and of all the four orders of men.
